name: v3 7% line, real money, 7% of exchange shard 0 available cash (compounding), no loss limit
status: FROZEN. Do not edit. Any change needs a new file and a new hash pinned in server/live/kalshi-pilot.js PILOT_SHA256 and test/kalshi-pilot.test.js.
source: Bryan, 2026-11-01: 'Ok time to set up live trading with Kalshi using the strategies v1 - v3'; pilot bankroll $100 total; go live with v3 only; 'I want it to be the 7% version'. 2026-11-01 (p2): $150 in the MAIN Kalshi account, use the full amount, no subaccount; reuse the desk's existing Kalshi key. Arming needs a separate message from Bryan and a typed phrase on the desk machine. 2026-11-01 (p3): 'I don't want it to only go off of 150. I wanted to go off of the full amount that's in the account... like it compounds.' The $150 bankroll cap is removed; $150 becomes a realized-loss limit. 2026-11-01 (p4): size from exchange shard 0 available cash only (GET /portfolio/balance?exchange_index=0, `balance`), not the combined cash and not portfolio_value. Bryan: 'I don't want there to be a loss cap... we're starting with 150 and that can go to zero I don't care but if it goes all the way up to 5000 and we're still going, let's still keep going. I don't want it to stop just because of this artificial little cap.' The realized-loss limit is removed; arm phrase is plain ARM LIVE.
money: integer cents for limits; Kalshi amounts parsed exactly to integer micro-dollars
bankrollRule: bankroll = the AVAILABLE CASH of exchange shard balanceExchangeIndex (GET /portfolio/balance?exchange_index=0, field `balance`, cents) + the pilot's own open cost (already out of cash), re-read before each decision (throttled refresh in shadow, a fresh read before every armed slice); no cap, so size compounds. Never the combined cash of all shards, never portfolio_value; pending deposits and other shards are display-only. No balance read: shadow skips the decision, armed halts. Shard cash below one contract: the pilot stops trading (plain status, not a halt).
account: main account (no subaccount): balance checks compare only the pilot's own fills and fees, never the absolute balance; other positions and orders are never managed or cancelled
openRiskRule: total open risk (the pilot's own open cost + fees) <= the live bankroll
dailyStopNote: OFF so live stays comparable with paper v3 (the paper arms have no daily stop). Code and tests exist; switching on (e.g. 1000 and true) needs a new file and hash.
dailyBudgetSizing: when shrinkToDailyBudget is true and a daily stop is set: before each slice, the worst-case loss (cost + fee if the contract settles NO) of the new contracts plus today's realized loss plus today's open worst-case must stay within the daily stop; size down, or skip if under 1 contract

order.hold: to settlement; the pilot never sells

fees.formula: per order: ceil_to_cent(0.07 * C * P * (1 - P)); real fees always come from Kalshi fill data

ordersRoute: create-order omits exchange_index, so Kalshi auto-routes by ticker to the market's own shard; any order reject (401/403, insufficient_balance, any other 4xx incl. 429) = one attempt then HALT, nothing else sent. A 429 on a READ (balance, deposits) is not a halt: back off and retry the read only
shardNote: CHECKED 2026-11-01: Kalshi's Exchange Sharding doc lists Crypto under shard 2 for new events, and the public GET /markets shows the open KXBTC15M, KXETH15M and KXSOL15M markets with exchange_index 2. Kalshi checks collateral on the market's own shard, and only App/Web orders auto-transfer cash between shards (API orders do not). So with balanceExchangeIndex 0 the first live order is expected to be rejected for insufficient balance unless shard 2 holds cash (or auto-rebalancing moves it); the pilot then halts after that one attempt. Changing the sizing shard needs a new file and hash.
stops: no loss limit: the pilot trades until HALT is pressed or a safety stop trips; the balance can go to zero. No per-trade dollar ceiling beyond the asset caps.
